blocks.headline: Jordan Falcon
blocks.subheadline:
I'm a software engineer with seven years of experience at ESPN and Disney, building responsive, accessible, and user-friendly digital experiences for sports fans. My background spans media, content management systems, consumer products, and high-traffic web applications.

Currently open to software engineering opportunities in New York City, hybrid, or remote.

blocks.title: About Me
blocks.body:
I'm a frontend-focused software engineer based in New York City with experience building digital products across sports, media, and technology.

My journey began in retail, where I advanced from a part-time sales associate to store manager at LIDS Sports Group within my first year. That experience taught me how to lead a team, understand customers, manage competing priorities, and connect everyday work to measurable business results.

I began college studying mechanical engineering at NYU Polytechnic School of Engineering before discovering that software development was where I could best combine creativity, problem-solving, and technology. I later studied computer science at CUNY Lehman College.

My early technology experience included working at The New York Times and Gestalt Interactive. I eventually joined ESPN as an intern and grew into a Software Engineer II, contributing to products and experiences used by sports fans across ESPN's digital platforms.

I enjoy transforming complex requirements into intuitive and reliable experiences while collaborating with designers, product managers, engineers, and other stakeholders.

Outside of coding, I enjoy sports, salsa dancing, gaming, creative design, and bringing people together through community events.

items.title: Where to Watch Guide
items.description: Helping fans discover when/where to watch. Built personalized viewing, filters, date-selection, league filtering, and responsive behavior.

caseStudy.project: A fan-facing guide that helps viewers find when and where to watch games, leagues, and live events across ESPN platforms.
caseStudy.problem: Fans struggled to discover viewing options quickly—filters, dates, and league context were fragmented and hard to personalize across devices.
caseStudy.myRole: Frontend engineer owning interactive filtering, personalized viewing flows, date selection, and responsive layout behavior.
caseStudy.actionsAndDecisions: Modeled filter and date state for predictable updates, wired league filtering into the guide experience, and prioritized mobile-first responsive patterns so discovery stayed usable on every screen size.
caseStudy.challenge: Keeping filter combinations, date ranges, and personalized defaults coherent without slowing the UI or overwhelming fans with options.
caseStudy.result: Shipped a clearer Where to Watch experience with personalized viewing, multi-filter discovery, and consistent responsive behavior.
caseStudy.learning: Discovery UIs succeed when state, filters, and layout decisions reinforce one mental model—especially under sports-calendar complexity.

items.title: Breaking News & Contributor Experiences
items.description: Built contributor pages, breaking-news carousel, follow-button functionality, and auth integration.

caseStudy.project: Contributor and breaking-news surfaces that surface trusted voices and urgent stories across ESPN publishing experiences.
caseStudy.problem: Contributor pages and breaking-news modules needed faster, more modular UI with follow/auth flows that still felt native to the site.
caseStudy.myRole: Built contributor page structure, the breaking-news carousel, follow-button behavior, and auth integration points.
caseStudy.actionsAndDecisions: Broke experiences into reusable components, optimized carousel and page performance, and integrated follow/auth so engagement actions stayed in-context.
caseStudy.challenge: Balancing publishing flexibility and performance while wiring auth-gated follow actions into high-traffic news surfaces.
caseStudy.result: Delivered contributor pages and breaking-news carousel experiences with follow functionality and auth integration.
caseStudy.learning: Component architecture and auth edges should be designed together so engagement features stay fast and coherent under publishing pressure.

items.title: DraftCast
items.description: Built Pick Predictor grid, Best Available, undo behavior, and completed-draft states for live draft experiences.

caseStudy.project: Live draft experiences where fans track picks, predictions, and board state as the draft unfolds in real time.
caseStudy.problem: Draft UIs needed reliable pick prediction, best-available views, undo paths, and clear completed-draft states under live data pressure.
caseStudy.myRole: Implemented Pick Predictor grid, Best Available views, undo behavior, and completed-draft state handling.
caseStudy.actionsAndDecisions: Used Redux-backed state for draft board updates, designed undo-friendly transitions, and defined completed-draft UI so the experience stayed readable after the final pick.
caseStudy.challenge: Keeping real-time draft state, undo, and prediction grids consistent when pick data arrives quickly and out of order.
caseStudy.result: Shipped DraftCast features that support live prediction, board clarity, and graceful end-of-draft states.
caseStudy.learning: Live sports UIs need explicit state machines for undo and completion—not just optimistic renders of the latest event.

items.title: ESPN Navigation
items.description: Improved navigation patterns for accessibility, clarity, and cross-platform consistency.

caseStudy.project: Navigation patterns used across ESPN experiences to help fans move between sports, scores, and content with less friction.
caseStudy.problem: Existing navigation patterns were inconsistent across platforms and created accessibility and clarity gaps for fans.
caseStudy.myRole: Improved navigation information architecture and interaction patterns with an accessibility-first lens.
caseStudy.actionsAndDecisions: Clarified hierarchy and labeling, strengthened keyboard and assistive-tech affordances, and aligned patterns for cross-platform consistency.
caseStudy.challenge: Improving accessibility and clarity without breaking established mental models fans already relied on.
caseStudy.result: Delivered clearer, more accessible navigation patterns with stronger cross-platform consistency.
caseStudy.learning: Navigation work is product strategy: accessibility and IA improvements compound when they are treated as shared system decisions.

items.title: Market Landing Pages
items.description: Shipped market-specific landing experiences with reusable modules and responsive layouts.

caseStudy.project: Market-specific landing experiences that localize ESPN storytelling and promotions for different audiences.
caseStudy.problem: Teams needed market landings that could vary by region without rebuilding layouts or sacrificing performance each time.
caseStudy.myRole: Shipped reusable landing modules and responsive layouts for market-specific experiences.
caseStudy.actionsAndDecisions: Designed modular page building blocks, kept layouts responsive by default, and prioritized performance so localized pages stayed fast.
caseStudy.challenge: Supporting market variation through reusable modules without letting CMS flexibility erode performance or design consistency.
caseStudy.result: Launched market landing pages built from reusable modules with responsive, performant layouts.
caseStudy.learning: CMS-driven landings scale when modules encode responsive and performance constraints—not just content slots.

items.title: GameCast
items.description: Contributed to live game experiences focused on clarity, speed, and fan-facing reliability.

caseStudy.project: Live game experiences that keep fans oriented around score, play, and context as games unfold.
caseStudy.problem: Live game surfaces must stay clear and reliable when data updates constantly and fans scan for the next meaningful signal.
caseStudy.myRole: Contributed to live GameCast experiences with focus on clarity, speed, and fan-facing reliability.
caseStudy.actionsAndDecisions: Prioritized readable live states, React patterns suited to frequent updates, and UX choices that surface the most important game signals first.
caseStudy.challenge: Maintaining clarity and perceived speed when live data volume and update frequency spike during high-stakes moments.
caseStudy.result: Helped deliver GameCast experiences oriented around clarity, speed, and reliable fan-facing updates.
caseStudy.learning: In live sports UI, restraint is a feature—showing the right signal at the right moment beats showing everything at once.
